_comment: Shared by core/src/snippets.rs tests and SnippetStore.selfTest (Swift).

cases._why: the trigger matches whatever case it was spoken in; the expansion keeps its own
a trigger inside a longer word must not expand
an empty trigger is skipped rather than matching everywhere
every trigger on a snippet expands to the same text: whisper writes a phrase several ways
cases.input: add my e-mail then add my e mail then add my email

cases._why: the longest trigger wins wherever two overlap, whatever order the rows were added in
cases.input: add my email signature and add my email

cases._why: a preset row the user has not filled in yet is inert: it must not delete the trigger
an expansion is never rescanned, so a trigger sitting inside canned text stays put
a dollar sign in an expansion is literal, not a regex capture reference

_protect_comment: Round-trips through expand/restore. {0}, {1} in `rewritten` stand for the nth sentinel; the test substitutes the real token. `expected: null` means the rewrite is discarded and the caller falls back to `expanded`.

protect._why: a rewrite that keeps the sentinels restores every expansion verbatim
protect.input: hey add my email and i will follow up
protect.expanded: hey ck@example.com and i will follow up
protect.rewritten: Hey, {0}, and I will follow up.
protect.expected: Hey, ck@example.com, and I will follow up.

protect._why: two expansions both survive a rewrite that reorders them
protect.input: add my email and add my site

protect._why: a rewrite that eats a sentinel is discarded whole, so the expansion still lands
protect.input: hey add my email and i will follow up
protect.expanded: hey ck@example.com and i will follow up

protect._why: no snippet fires: there is nothing to protect and the rewrite is kept as-is
